extracted.intended_audience: academics and administrators involved in peer review (faculty, fellowship/grant panel members, graduate students, deans/provosts) and readers interested in the sociology of expert judgment
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards used by professors and review panels to evaluate scholarly work (papers, proposals, fellowships, grants), with attention to disciplinary differences, fairness, and the interpersonal processes of deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the research original and important?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented in the text as a core question reviewers must decide; central to judgments of 'excellence.' Panels ask whether the work represents new contribution and substantive importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual boldness (brave vs. glib)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators distinguish genuine intellectual risk-taking from superficial or glib claims; bravery implies substantive, well-defended innovation rather than flashy or shallow argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and lasting relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether a project addresses timely and enduring problems versus following short-lived fashions; the page frames this as a criterion for judging quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and inclusiveness (pro-diversity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book raises whether work promotes diversity or is evaluated in ways that consider gender, ethnic, and other diversity dimensions; personal and institutional preferences about diversity influence decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels evaluate whether cross-disciplinary work meets standards across fields and whether it successfully integrates methods/insights; the text highlights difficulties in multidisciplinary review and the need to decide which standard applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary standards and methodological fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Different disciplines have distinctive standards (e.g., economists prefer mathematical models; historians favor kinds of evidence; philosophers may prioritize being intelligible to their peers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers judge methodological appropriateness and fit with disciplinary norms; when members from multiple disciplines convene, they are expected to explain and respect these differing standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to explain their criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels should articulate the standards they use for judgment so deliberations are accountable and comprehensible across disciplinary lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should respect each other's expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberations require deference to domain experts when appropriate; panels must balance cross-disciplinary critique with acknowledgment of specialized knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding similarity bias (homophily)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guard against admiring only work that resembles their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book highlights a common anti-pattern: reviewers favor work similar to their own research. Panels should actively guard against this tendency to ensure fair assessment of novel or different approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of emotional, cognitive, and social influences
rubrics_metrics.description: Judging quality isn't robotically rational; it's emotional, cognitive, and social, too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should recognize that emotions, cognitive heuristics, and social dynamics shape judgments and account for these factors when evaluating work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical rigor and capacity to analyze complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Professors' self-respect is rooted in their ability to analyze complexity and recognize quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality evaluations rely on careful, nuanced analysis rather than surface judgments; reviewers' skill at parsing complexity is a criterion for good evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to overcoming biases and fair process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers strive to identify the best proposals and try to overcome their own biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes that reviewers' efforts to mitigate bias and their commitment to the review process contribute to fairer outcomes; deliberate anti-bias practices are implied as positive standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building a culture of multidisciplinary discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels must cultivate norms of discourse so committees can decide which standard is best in multidisciplinary review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In multidisciplinary panels, a deliberate culture of discussion is necessary to negotiate and select appropriate evaluative standards; procedural norms for deliberation matter for outcome quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of political and knowledge consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation decisions have political and knowledge consequences affecting how excellence is judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be mindful of broader ramifications (institutional, political, epistemic) of awarding prestige or resources, since these consequences shape scholarly fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpersonal processes and deliberation quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpersonal processes make review panels work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group dynamics, respect, argument quality, and deliberative practices influence decisions; managing these interpersonal factors is part of producing fair and robust evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity, fairness, and neutral analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Professors pride themselves on objectivity, fairness to competing views, or at least capacity for neutral analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for impartiality and balanced consideration of competing perspectives; recognize limits of pure objectivity while striving for fair treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of institutional mechanics shaping outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes of peer review are shaped by institutional mechanics as much as by reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and administrators should account for procedural and institutional factors (e.g., norms, power structures) that influence decisions, and seek reforms that improve fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reflection and gatekeeper accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Gatekeepers (reviewers, panel chairs) should better understand and perform their role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book urges those running and participating in peer review to reflect on practices, biases, and responsibilities and to improve evaluative conduct and accountability.
